hesitations.reason: Step 4 gives both: the pistols can hit only infantry and official text praises them against infantry, while official text also says even the mightiest tanks fall to her charges. The largest bonus cannot be told, so I followed the step's fallback, the target official text names first; the profile and history name infantry (conscripts) first.

Anti-armour holds only because the C4 is coded armour-piercing (see armament/1/damage). I considered infiltrator for the buildings she blows up, but the infiltrator / anti-armour tie-break keeps infiltrator for spying, theft and sabotage from inside, and her charges are set from outside. Raider and scout fail their requires (she is medium speed). Recorded in uncertain.

Both are t3 gates in the tier_map and she needs both at 1.12. The RA3 note says only that she is t3 either way. The 'record the highest tech building' note is written for RA1/RA2. I picked the Defense Bureau because the registry suggestion gives it to the other units that need both, such as the FutureTank X-1. The Boot camp page lists only Max Clearance (uncertain, sources_disagree).

Decided by the soldier rule. Her infobox names no armour set; one changelog line (beta 1.5) halves explosive damage to her, while the Conscript's set takes explosives in full. The rule does not say whether one known resistance, with the rest of her set unknown, counts as tougher armour than the basic rifle infantry.

There is no damage category, so step 5 applies. I took the armour-piercing exception because the sources present the charges as how she kills tanks and ships (official text; the patch 1.05 cursor over vehicles and ships). But the charges are just as much her anti-building tool, and the Boot camp line stresses buildings, which argues for the default. This choice also decides whether the anti-armour secondary role meets its requires.
The source is clear that she must reach the target and plant the charge by hand. The melee coding rule and the melee/short tie-break speak of blows, leaps and latches, not of a placed charge.

No source says the charges cannot be used on infantry, and step 4 fills unstated kinds. I left infantry out because every source pairs the charges with buildings, vehicles and ships, and the patch 1.05 C4 cursor shows only on vehicles and ships.

Step 3 needs a label by target. The anti-infantry label sits on the Multigunner IFV's copy of her guns, which that page says has identical stats, not on her own weapon. StrategyWiki rules out aircraft.
The rule was clear but the source was silent on how the shots travel, so I used the family default.

The Time Belt restores health and moves her, but only back to her own earlier state. Neither pattern gives the same counterplay (kill her inside the window, or camp the spot she returns to), so by the pattern-link test I linked neither.

new_mechanics.summary: On a key, the unit snaps back to where it stood, at the health it had, a few seconds earlier, undoing damage and movement since, then waits out a recharge. Counterplay: burst it down inside the window or while the key recharges, freeze or disable it so it cannot use the key, or wait at the spot it will snap back to.

On a key, shrink one enemy vehicle or ship for a time: it moves and fires faster but deals a fraction of its damage, reaches and sees less, takes double damage and can be crushed by any crushing vehicle (infantry are immune). Counterplay: pull the shrunk unit back until the effect wears off, keep crushers away from it, or shoot down the caster, which cannot fight back.
